composition.title: Hospital discharge report (synthetic): fracture of the left kneecap, Reykjavik

items.label: No NSAIDs: on an anticoagulant, with hypertension
High fall risk: knee brace, walking frame and left-sided weakness

sections.title: Hospital course
sections.narrative: An elderly Swedish visitor slipped on ice and was brought to the emergency department with a painful, swollen left knee. X-ray showed a displaced transverse fracture of the patella. His Swedish patient summary, read before surgery, showed a penicillin allergy and treatment with insulin, a blood-pressure medicine and an oral anticoagulant. The anticoagulant was paused, and the fracture was fixed the next day by open reduction and tension band wiring under spinal anaesthesia, with clindamycin as prophylaxis. The course after surgery was uneventful: plasma glucose 9 to 14 mmol/L on his usual basal insulin with correction doses, haemoglobin 118 g/L, the anticoagulant restarted the evening after surgery. He was mobilised with a walking frame and a hinged knee brace locked in extension. Simulated episode for an invented person.

items.label: Closed fracture of the left patella (kneecap)
items.note: Transverse, displaced. Fall due to slipping on ice (SNOMED CT 242387001) in Reykjavik. Treated with open reduction and internal fixation.

items.label: Open reduction and internal fixation of the left patella (tension band wiring)
items.note: Spinal anaesthesia. No complications. Hinged knee brace fitted after surgery.

items.label: Paracetamol
items.detail: 1 g by mouth up to 4 times daily, at least 6 hours apart

items.label: Oxycodone
items.detail: 5 mg by mouth when needed, at most 4 times daily, for at most 7 days after discharge
items.note: New at discharge, short course. Caution: emphysema, age and a high fall risk. No NSAIDs.

items.label: Oral anticoagulant (the patient's existing treatment)
items.detail: Usual dose, restarted the evening after surgery
items.note: Existing treatment, paused before surgery and restarted. Thromboprophylaxis: no low-molecular-weight heparin was added, because the existing anticoagulant covers it. The Swedish health centre should confirm the dose and the plan at follow-up.

items.label: Insulin (the patient's existing treatment)
items.detail: Usual basal dose; correction doses were given in hospital
items.note: Existing treatment, continued. Plasma glucose was 9 to 14 mmol/L after surgery. Closer glucose follow-up is recommended while the patient is immobile.

items.label: Clindamycin
items.detail: 600 mg intravenously, one dose before surgery
items.note: Surgical prophylaxis, chosen because of the penicillin allergy. Completed.

items.label: Penicillin
items.note: Known from the patient's Swedish patient summary, read through HIP before surgery. Surgical prophylaxis was therefore clindamycin, not a beta-lactam.

steps.text: Knee brace for 6 weeks, locked in extension when walking
Range of motion 0 to 30 degrees in weeks 1 and 2, then increased step by step to 90 degrees by week 6
Isometric quadriceps exercises and straight leg raises from day 1
Wound check and removal of sutures 14 days after surgery
Control X-ray of the knee 6 weeks after surgery
Plasma glucose before meals and at bedtime for 2 weeks
Review of the insulin doses by the diabetes nurse within 1 week
Home blood pressure once daily for 2 weeks
Review of the blood-pressure treatment when the pain treatment ends
Confirm the anticoagulant dose and the bleeding risk at the first follow-up

sections.title: Discharge details
sections.narrative:
Discharged in a stable condition to travel home to Sweden with an escort. Walks short distances with a walking frame and the knee brace; needs help on stairs. Pain controlled with paracetamol and a short course of oxycodone. The wound is dry. Follow-up at his Swedish health centre within one week.
Discharged to travel home to Sweden; follow-up at the patient's Swedish health centre.
